project_constraints: Real-VMS evidence outranks assumptions encoded in mocks; where they disagree, the cluster is right and the mock is a bug.
Mock behavior must remain evidence-based: model observed cluster shapes, never invent semantics.

NFSv4.1 lab validation targets the VMS that owns the mounted NFSv4.1 filesystem - currently var204.selab.vastdata.com (available since 2026-08-18, VAST 5.5.0). var203 (5.4.6) remains the target for the other protocols' lab validation. A lab workflow must verify mount-to-VMS consistency before collecting evidence.
Re-measure before optimizing; request volume is a first-class regression dimension.
Credentials are environment-sourced (VAST_PASSWORD / VAST_TOKEN); never in argv, files, logs, or documentation.
Never enumerate-and-delete unrelated adhoc_opstat_* monitors; cleanup is exact-id only.
Do not rerun tests merely to turn an unexplained flake green; capture the failing output instead.
Known flake on record: test_smb_merged_monitor_single_query_per_refresh failed once, unreproduced, on Python 3.8; if it recurs, capture the evidence rather than hiding it.
Interactive responsiveness still lacks a committed PTY benchmark harness; interactive claims are unproven without a PTY run or a real-cluster session.

Lab workflows that depend on a workload declare and verify the required load generator BEFORE evidence collection: fail immediately when absent, name the missing prerequisite, show the operator the start command, and never auto-start/stop services or manufacture workload state.

items.title: NFSv3 VIEW attribution / host_view rebuild
items.summary: Decide with evidence whether the NFSv3 VIEW drill should be rebuilt around the exporter's host_view series, which carries protocol=NFS3, instead of ViewMetrics.
scope: Inspect the current NFSv3 VIEW attribution path (ViewMetrics).
Characterize host_view with protocol=NFS3 on a real cluster.
Compare attribution correctness between the two sources.
Compare API cost, drill-entry cost and steady-state cost.
Determine whether host_view should replace or augment the current path.
If implementation changes, model the proven real payload shape in the mock.
Real-VMS validate any implementation change.
acceptance_criteria: An evidence-backed decision to retain the current architecture or move NFSv3 VIEW attribution to host_view.
Correctness and API-efficiency comparison results recorded.
evidence: Current NFSv3 VIEW path still uses ViewMetrics.
The NFSv4.1 host_view rebuild may be portable.
Recorded at milestone close as the largest remaining honest-telemetry opportunity.

2026-08-17 real-VMS run (var203/5.4.6, HEAD fa79751): host_view publishes NO NFS series under any protocol label (0 matches in the raw exposition) while heavy live NFSv3 fio traffic was proven running - only BLOCK/NDB/S3/SMB2 appear. The 'host_view carries protocol=NFS3' premise is build-dependent and FALSE on 5.4.6; a rebuild/hybrid on host_view is not viable on the supported cluster.

Same run: ViewMetrics view-scope batch monitor (8 views, one create, no_aggregation) worked correctly and returned measured zeros - but the probe monitored head-of-list idle views, not the loadgen's /kmacs view, so whether ViewMetrics attributes the NFSv3 load remains the one open FR1 fact.

2026-08-17 targeted pass (HEAD 0bced30): NFSv3 workload PROVEN in-window by client mountstats deltas over the 130 s probe (READ 12,273/s, WRITE 6,613/s, plus GETATTR/SETATTR/LOOKUP/CREATE/REMOVE/MKDIR activity) against mount 172.200.202.6:/kmacs (vers=3).

/views/ is a complete bare-list response (239,857 bytes, 147 views, no pagination). No view object has path /kmacs or /kmacs/nfstest - the NFSv3 export maps into the ROOT view (path /, id 1, protocols NFS+NFS4), so per-view NFSv3 attribution is structurally coarse on this cluster layout.

One rank monitor covered all 147 views; the root view scored ~0 while ~18,900 NFSv3 ops/s flowed, and the top-ranked views were SMB/BLOCK/S3/NDB. Strong evidence ViewMetrics does not attribute NFSv3 on 5.4.6 (mirror of D-006's NFSv4 finding), and CONFIRMED that the production NFSv3 VIEW drill's own ranking surfaces other-protocol views inside an NFSv3 screen.
Neither ViewMetrics nor TenantMetrics carries any NFS protocol discriminator in the catalog; host_view has no NFS series. No source on 5.4.6 can answer 'which views carry NFSv3 right now' per-view.

2026-08-17 FINAL surgical evidence (lab run fr3-fr1-20260817-220404): with id anchors pinning BOTH path-'/' view objects and client mountstats proving ~12,600 READ/s + 6,800 WRITE/s NFSv3 through the root namespace during the window, ViewMetrics reported id 1 at 0.03 md-ops/s with zero data IOPS/BW, and id 217 at zero across 10 samples. Combined with host_view publishing no NFS series and ViewMetrics having no protocol discriminator: NO VALID NFSV3 VIEW ATTRIBUTION SOURCE ON VAST 5.4.6. The current NFSv3 VIEW drill surfaces other protocols' busiest views under an NFSv3 heading (rank evidence, two runs).

2026-08-17 Stage B REAL-VMS VALIDATED (run fr1-20260817-224726, HEAD 6e6fe15): all 13 production-path checks PASS on var203 under proven live NFSv3 load (23,303 client ops in window). Rendered frame shows exactly the D-016 notice with full canonical footer and live NFSv3 headline beneath; zero foreign-protocol view rows; the whole session cost 5 API calls with ZERO /views/ fetches, zero rank/display monitors for VIEW entry; exit returned to the dashboard; the single headline monitor was deleted and 404-verified. Whole-run artifact policy clean (API log in-tree, no new /tmp files). FR1 complete; future NFS3 host_view support remains a capability-driven opportunity behind view_attribution_source() (D-016), not unfinished FR1 work.
notes: 2026-08-17: grouped with FR3 into the Telemetry Correctness milestone (coordinated investigation; shared host_view evidence).

2026-08-17 owner decision language: PROVISIONAL KEEP VIEWMETRICS - HIGH confidence that a host_view REBUILD/HYBRID is not viable on 5.4.6 (no NFS host_view series); MEDIUM confidence that ViewMetrics is the final solution, pending the busy-view test (probe never exercised the actual active NFSv3 view).

2026-08-17 targeted-pass verdict: leaning NO VALID NFSV3 VIEW ATTRIBUTION SOURCE ON 5.4.6, pending one surgical check (display-monitor the root view id 1 under load; rank evidence already says ~0). Probe imperfections recorded: --view-paths anchors require exact match and skip silently; duplicate view paths resolve to the last-listed id (id 217 was monitored for '/', not id 1).

2026-08-17: surgical check prepared - probe --view-ids 1,217 pins both path-'/' view objects; committed lab script scripts/opstat-lab-fr3-fr1-validation.sh runs it under proven NFSv3 load with client-side mountstats deltas. Expected outcome ~0 ViewMetrics activity on both, finalizing NO VALID NFSV3 VIEW ATTRIBUTION SOURCE ON 5.4.6.

2026-08-17: recommended product direction (NOT yet implemented, awaiting owner approval): honest unavailable-state notice on builds without a valid source (D-009/NVMe dead-scope pattern), with future capability detection - use host_view protocol=NFS3 when a build publishes it (5.5.0.1-class evidence) and fall back to the honest notice otherwise. Explicit all-protocol relabel rejected as primary: it keeps a misleading-adjacent panel under an NFSv3 screen while SMB/S3 engines already own their per-protocol view drills.

2026-08-17 Stage A: honest unavailable state IMPLEMENTED (bb6061d) - capability seam view_attribution_source(), zero-API-cost VIEW entry, notice-not-error rendering, D-016 recorded; view-row builder regressions preserved as pure vast_drill tests and engine protections converted to the tenant drill; large-population coverage remains in SMB/S3/NVMe suites. Real-VMS validation pending via scripts/opstat-lab-fr1-unavailable-validation.sh (in-process production-path validator, mock-proven 13/13). FR1 moves to done only on returned Stage-B evidence.
2026-08-17: DONE - Telemetry Correctness milestone complete (FR1 + FR3).

2026-08-18 (manual-testing pass): nfs_v3.view_attribution_source() still returns the deliberate D-016 capability result, so [v] renders the honest unavailable notice on every build. Making it a dynamic probe remains a KNOWN FUTURE VALIDATION OPPORTUNITY behind that seam, gated on real-VMS evidence from a 5.5.0.1-class cluster that publishes protocol-labeled host_view NFS series - not unfinished work, and not a new FR (D-016 already records the reopening condition).

items.title: Prominent startup/warm-up UX for slow-to-first-data telemetry paths
items.summary: Defensive UX: when first meaningful numbers legitimately take a long time (slow cluster/API periods), the user must immediately see a prominent, plain-English explanation that opstat is connected and preparing data - never a mostly empty screen that looks hung.
scope: Prominent plain-English startup/warm-up panel shown immediately at launch and through the warm-up window (between first paint and first meaningful numbers), clearing automatically when real data lands.

Communicate in user language: connected; performance monitoring being prepared; data actively being collected; some statistics need multiple measurements before they can be shown accurately; initial startup may take about a minute on some systems; the screen populates automatically; continuous updates follow.
No implementation jargon: no monitor ids, REST endpoints, property families, or VMS monitor architecture in user-facing text.
Only claim durations that are truthful for the engine/cluster (e.g. 'about a minute' where measured).

Applies to any engine during genuinely slow warm-ups. Normal startup is fast (measured 2026-08-17: SMB usable in ~8 s, Block/NVMe dashboard in ~12 s); the same serial work measured 58-157 s on the same cluster during high-latency periods (rounds 2-5B), which is the case this UX exists for. Footer and existing phase messages preserved.
Render-path tests for the new warm-up state (footer survival, width, clear-on-data).
acceptance_criteria: During a real slow startup the user sees, from the first seconds, a prominent explanation meeting the communication goals above, with no implementation jargon.
The explanation clears automatically when meaningful data displays, and normal refresh behavior is unchanged.
Footer renders in the warm-up state at every width; covered by render tests on both interpreters.
No change to VMS REST API behavior, call counts, or timing.
evidence: Rounds 2-5B measured NVMe startup at 58-157 s of honest serial VMS REST time (8 monitor creates + 8 first queries at 2-38 s per call on var203), plus a two-measurement warm-up for counter-based rows.
Owner acceptance pass (2026-08-17): SMB and Block/NVMe both exceeded one minute to useful telemetry; the existing phase messages were not enough to make the wait legible.
Need is established by Block/NVMe alone; independent of the separate SMB startup attribution measurement.

2026-08-17 remeasurement: SMB startup completed its four expected VMS REST calls in ~1.02 s with a usable screen in ~8 s; Block/NVMe dashboard in ~12 s with valid telemetry and an honest warming-up marker. The earlier >60 s observations were transient environmental/VMS latency, not reproducible product behavior - hence defensive priority, not priority 2.
notes: Starting-point copy (to refine): 'Preparing performance data... opstat is connected and setting up performance monitoring with the cluster. Some statistics require multiple measurements before they can be displayed accurately. Initial startup may take about a minute. Once ready, this screen will update continuously.'

Re-prioritized 2 -> 12 on 2026-08-17 owner decision: normal startup is 8-12 s, so this is defensive UX for slow periods. Natural delivery affinity with FR7 (release/product hardening); kept as its own FR so the scope and copy survive intact.

items.title: NFSv4.1 delegation diagnostic
items.summary: Complete the intentionally deferred delegation diagnostic: on-demand, file/path-scoped delegation visibility with zero cost on the normal refresh path.
scope: Design a path-entry or path-selection interaction.
Query delegation state only on explicit request.
Keep the diagnostic off the normal refresh path.
Add mock coverage.
Validate against real VMS.
acceptance_criteria: A user can explicitly inspect delegation information for a file/path without adding API cost to normal NFSv4.1 polling.
evidence: Delegation visibility needs a file/path-scoped interaction and must remain on-demand (D-008).
The nfs4_delegs DELETE sibling must never be invoked; a test asserts it is not.

2026-08-17 discovery pass 1 (var203/5.4.6, HEAD 5c7eb30): GET /tenants/{id}/nfs4_delegs/ EXISTS on 5.4.6 and still requires file_path (HTTP 400 'field required' without it, consistently). GET-only contract held; lab artifact policy clean (API log in-tree, /tmp unchanged).

Pass 1 was inconclusive on record shape: no real file candidate was discovered (loadgen in a sleep phase; *.bin glob empty), and guessed directory paths queried against the first three tenants in API order (37/25/51) all returned HTTP 400 get_handle_by_path GetHandleByPathCode.ILLEGAL_PATH - evidence of wrong-tenant/wrong-target queries, NOT an endpoint defect. Correct view->tenant correlation and a real existing file are prerequisites; record fields, empty-success shape and pagination semantics remain unproven.

2026-08-18: second corrected lab attempt at 3f2627d was INVALID as FR2 evidence - the committed lab script passed --evidence-dir to a probe parser that no longer accepted it (a refactor dropped the argument; no gate test exercised the script-to-probe CLI contract), so the probe exited at argparse (rc 2) before any endpoint query. No FR2 endpoint conclusion was drawn from that run. Artifact routing itself remained compliant with the no-/tmp policy. Fixed: build_parser() contract factored and regression-tested against the committed script's actual argv; candidate discovery rebuilt (open-fd scan of any process, command-line-derived paths, walk keeping zero-byte files - the nfs41 loadgen uses no fio, and the size filter cost the trip its candidates); the script now refuses to run the probe without a proven real file and exits nonzero with a RUN FAILED banner while still packaging failure evidence.

2026-08-18 CORRECTION (owner): the lab server's NFSv4.1 mount (172.200.204.6:/kmacs/nfstest) belongs to VAR204, not var203 - the 2026-08-18 discovery run queried var203's nfs4_delegs about files living on another cluster. ALL ILLEGAL_PATH responses from the var203 runs are therefore INVALID for judging nfs4_delegs path semantics or 5.4.6 release behavior (superseding the earlier path-semantics inference). Still valid from those runs: GET-only safety held, candidate discovery found real files, view/tenant derivation executed as designed, artifact policy clean, errors preserved verbatim. This was a lab-targeting defect; the corrected workflow defaults NFSv4.1 discovery to var204 and hard-fails on mount-to-VMS mismatch (verified against the target cluster's own VIP inventory, not string guessing).

2026-08-18 DECISIVE var204 discovery (run fr2-var204-20260818-194511, HEAD fbcc583, VAST 5.5.0.1): mount-to-VMS consistency PASS (172.200.204.6 is a var204 VIP); exact view 755 /kmacs/nfstest, tenant 1 default. Proven wire contract: GET /tenants/{tid}/nfs4_delegs/?file_path=<FULL NAMESPACE PATH, leading slash, URL-encoded>. Valid file with no delegation and a directory both return HTTP success with delegate_info=[] and count_total=0; a nonexistent path returns HTTP 400 get_handle_by_path ILLEGAL_PATH (so 'no delegation' and 'bad path' are distinguishable and must stay distinct in UX). FIVE live WRITE delegation records captured; proven record shape: client_id int, delegation_client_ip str, delegation_stateid int, delegation_type str, revoke_in_progress bool, vip_addr str - client ip matched the real mounted client, vip_addr matched the mount VIP. Wrapper carries xeystore_pagination (false observed) and xeystore_pagination_next_client_id (populated even when pagination is false). File-scoped GETs 217-709 ms; the no-file_path 400 took ~1.8 s. GET-only safety held (zero non-GET lines). Supersedes the path-semantics uncertainty: the full namespace path is the source of truth; D-008's on-demand-only architecture stands (zero delegation calls on the normal refresh path).

2026-08-18 IMPLEMENTATION (mock/unit proven, real-VMS validation pending): production diagnostic shipped in nfs_v41.py per the owner-approved design - [d] Delegation prompt (full namespace path, leading /, no guessing; Enter submits, Enter/Backspace on empty cancels, Ctrl-U clears; bare Esc is stripped by the terminal layer so it cannot cancel - documented deviation), prompt-first dispatch plus a prompt-aware quit guard (_should_quit: typing q/d/x/v/h inside a path is text), tenant resolution from the real view inventory via shared vast_drill.namespace_candidate_views/_tenants (exact non-root view authoritative with NO fallback on ILLEGAL_PATH; root-only prefix allows ONE bounded fallback; >3 distinct tenants is honest ambiguity, never a spray), GET-only _deleg_lookup_get with no method parameter (D-008), proven six-field record model rendered as four primary fields plus one dim client_id/stateid line, live/empty/invalid/invalid-input/unavailable/ambiguous/error/malformed states with zero-vs-unavailable kept distinct, 8-row bound with an honest truncation notice (xeystore_pagination or count_total), [space] manual re-query only, zero delegation calls on the normal refresh path, session-cached /views/ (<=1 fetch + <=2 delegation GETs per lookup). Footer gained [d]; _MAX_FRAME_WIDTH raised 140->152 deliberately (legend measures 147+4). Mock upgraded to the proven wire contract (tenant fields on views, six-field records, ILLEGAL_PATH rule). 105 new tests in tests/test_deleg_diagnostic.py cover the full owner matrix; suite 768 passed / 0 skipped on the dev interpreter pre-gate.

2026-08-18 SPECIALIST REVIEW PASS (api-efficiency, telemetry-semantics, tui-render, all read-only): blocking/high findings fixed before commit - (1) dispatch_queued_keys lowercased the whole key buffer, silently rewriting case-sensitive namespace paths typed into the prompt; keys now deliver case-preserved and every engine folds case in its command branch only, with wire-path regression tests driving dispatch_queued_keys with mixed case; (2) a buffered 'd<path with q>' single read still quit - _should_quit now simulates prompt state across the buffer; (3) the truncation notice claimed the cluster held more than the diagnostic fetched even when the display bound was the only truncation - notice now split by cause, pagination flag named not interpreted, derived counts phrased as returned not reported; (4) delegation frames overflowed below 40 columns - box_top now truncates titles and the width matrix extends to 24/10; also: empty-state directory caveat made unconditional (the capture's directory path had no trailing slash), 404/invalid messages carry provenance (tenant names), prompt/result paths keep their tail visible, loading-order tests added for both blocking paths, Rule B 2-GET budget proven over the wire. Wire contract + unproven payload aspects recorded in D-017.

2026-08-18 STAGE B REAL-VMS VALIDATION PASS (run fr2val-var204-20260818-205116, validated SHA 5fd6909, var204 selab-var-204, VAST 5.5.0.1, RESULT: PASS, VALIDATOR-RC 0, script failures 0; raw-first review confirmed the archive agrees with the validator summary): the production nfs_v41 diagnostic, driven in-process through _dispatch_key, validated end to end - [d] discoverable and opens the prompt with the footer intact; q typed in the prompt is path text; cancel works. A real workload file (/kmacs/nfstest/nfs41_loadgen/attr_stress.txt, derived live from the loadgen) returned a live WRITE delegation with all six proven fields populated; delegation_client_ip 172.200.14.198 equals the mount's own clientaddr and vip_addr 172.200.204.6 equals the mount VIP; answering tenant recorded as default; frame rendered the four primary fields plus the dim client_id/stateid line with '1 delegation(s) reported'. Export root /kmacs/nfstest returned state=empty rendered as information with the directory caveat (valid-empty vs invalid distinction real-VMS proven); nonexistent path returned the literal ILLEGAL_PATH 400 and rendered state=invalid with footer. API cost: first lookup 1 /views/ + 1 delegation GET; repeat lookup 0 /views/ (session cache); [space] exactly 1 delegation GET and 0 other calls; 3 poll ticks with a result on screen made 0 delegation calls - zero-normal-refresh-cost is real-VMS validated. Safety: API log holds 5 nfs4_delegs calls, all GET, 0 DELETE/POST/PUT/PATCH (D-008 honored); the one POST/DELETE pair is the engine's own headline monitor 330, deleted with HTTP 204 and confirmed gone by per-id GET (note: that verification GET runs after cleanup() closes the API log, so its 404 is recorded in validator-output.txt, not the log). Artifact policy clean: evidence in the DTS tree, /tmp before/after identical, ZIP integrity + SHA256 produced. VALIDATED SCOPE: full-namespace-path input, exact/prefix tenant resolution, live rendering, valid-empty and invalid-path distinctions, GET-only safety, manual re-query, zero timed-refresh cost, bounded lookups - on VAST 5.5.0.1/var204 ONLY; VAST 5.4.6 remains outside the validated scope.
notes: 2026-08-17: Bundle 1 begins - Stage A repository/API analysis; design-first per owner instruction, D-008 governs.

2026-08-18: owner approved implementation with five product decisions: (1) [d] 'Delegation', NFSv4.1 footer only; (2) V1 input is the full VAST namespace path only; (3) refined tenant resolution A-D (exact view = authoritative no-fallback, root-prefix = one bounded fallback, record the answering tenant, honest ambiguity, never spray); (4) [space] = manual re-query only, no timed refresh, zero normal-refresh delegation cost; (5) client_id/delegation_stateid as one dim secondary line, no detail toggle. FR2 remains in_progress until scripts/opstat-lab-fr2-delegation-validation.sh passes on var204 (production in-process validator scripts/var203_validation/validate_fr2_delegation.py; minimum success = live records on a real workload file with an all-PASS run).

2026-08-18: FR2 closed on Stage-B evidence. The Stage-A discovery history stands unrewritten: original D-008 evidence, the invalid var203 cross-cluster targeting runs (reclassified, not deleted), the corrected decisive var204 discovery, D-017, and this final production validation. The layered lab-script prerequisite model (service -> mount health -> mount-to-VMS consistency -> workload evidence -> validator) is now proven in practice by this run. Discovery and validation scripts are retained as durable revalidation tooling.

items.title: Latency source-unit certainty
items.summary: Remove the remaining uncertainty about native latency units; every user-visible latency source gets a proven unit, explicit conversion and literal regression tests.
scope: Create targeted probes instead of depending on generic validator timing.
Deliberately generate/select traffic that produces a usable non-zero known-microseconds reference.
Prove the native unit of each unresolved source: NVMe BlockMetrics, VolumeMetrics, host_view latency, SMB per-operation, S3 per-operation.
Lock conversion paths with literal tests.
Add or update a decision record if warranted.
acceptance_criteria: Every user-visible latency source has a proven native unit, explicit conversion, explicit display unit, and literal regression tests.
evidence: Nfs4Metrics latency is proven microseconds.
Three generic cross-check attempts failed to produce a useful non-zero known-microseconds reference (idle NFS4 windows).
Magnitude alone is not proof; displays remain unchanged and marked UNVERIFIED until evidence is decisive.

2026-08-17 real-VMS run: the /metrics/ catalog carries a per-metric 'units' field, but it labels *_latency__avg 'ms' uniformly INCLUDING the D-003-proven-raw-microseconds NFS4Common metric, and is self-inconsistent (KafkaViewMetrics/qos 'us') - it reflects the VMS UI display convention, not the wire value. Exporter # HELP text and the 19.6 MB swagger carry no unit information. Mechanism A is exhausted.

Block pairing, 20 paired nonzero samples: BlockMetrics read_latency__avg 576.6-683.1 (median 619.5) vs vast_host_view_latency BLOCK 0.811-0.873 (median 0.838); ratio 663-815, median 739, mean 745 +/- 46. Only consistent with BlockMetrics=us and host_view=ms (a ~0.74 semantic factor from combined-vs-read-only latency and differing windows); rules out same-unit and ns. host_view-as-us is CONTRADICTED.

The planned decisive NFS4 same-family proof is impossible on var203: host_view has no NFS series on 5.4.6. Strongest remaining local proof: pair vast_host_view_read_latency (same op class, present in the raw exposition but not parsed by production) against BlockMetrics read_latency__avg, plus client-side fio latency from the block loadgen.

VolumeMetrics,read_latency__avg at cluster scope is NOT queryable on 5.4.6: monitor created (HTTP 201) but every query returned HTTP 400 'metrics not available' (property_error) - 20/20. The probe summary line 'never nonzero' understated this; the raw API log is authoritative.

2026-08-17 targeted pass: SAME-OP-CLASS pairing - BlockMetrics,read_latency__avg vs raw vast_host_view_read_latency (BLOCK) - 6 paired nonzero samples: 581.33-727.01 vs constant 0.64; ratio min 908.3 / max 1136.0 / median 969.1 / mean 987.6. VERY STRONG EVIDENCE: host_view latency gauges are milliseconds, BlockMetrics microseconds. Implementation may proceed on this; no further real-VMS evidence required for the FR3 host_view fix.

VolumeMetrics at VOLUME scope (2 of 16 volumes): queries succeeded (no property_error, unlike cluster scope) but every sample returned no complete value in the window - queryable, unit still unproven.

2026-08-17 REAL-VMS VALIDATED (lab run fr3-fr1-20260817-220404, HEAD 4374f21): the implemented D-014 conversion verified against live data - raw hv_read 0.59-0.65 vs BlockMetrics 577-651 (6 pairs, ratio 902.7-1032.9, median 913.6, re-confirming ms); production parse_host_view produced 787.7 us vs BlockMetrics 581.1 us (combined-vs-read ratio 0.69, same microsecond band) - the ~1000x understatement is eliminated through the real production parser path. fr3.production_conversion PASS; exact-id cleanup PASS. Final unit ledger: Nfs4Metrics us PROVEN (D-003); NFS4Common us PROVEN; host_view ms VERY STRONG EVIDENCE + implemented (D-014); BlockMetrics us VERY STRONG EVIDENCE (no display change needed); SMB/S3 ProtoMetrics us STRONG INFERENCE; SmbMetrics/S3Metrics/ViewMetrics/TenantMetrics per-op us ASSUMED (displays already consistent, no change warranted); VolumeMetrics UNKNOWN (cluster scope unqueryable, volume scope null-valued in sampled windows). Catalog units field is display convention (D-015).
notes: 2026-08-17: grouped with FR1 into the Telemetry Correctness milestone (coordinated investigation; shared host_view evidence).

2026-08-17: host_view latency unit -> CONTRADICTORY-to-current-code (strong inference: ms). Production nfs4_native stores it as latency_us and nfs_v41 h/v drills format it as microseconds - a likely ~1000x understatement on builds where NFS host_view series exist (e.g. 5.5.0.1); on 5.4.6 those panels render their honest empty state, so the defect is latent on var203.

2026-08-17: D-014 fix IMPLEMENTED - parse_host_view converts the ms gauge to us at ingestion; decision records D-014 (host_view latency is milliseconds) and D-015 (catalog units field is display convention) recorded; literal regression test pins 0.64 -> 640 us. Real-VMS validation of the implemented conversion rides in scripts/opstat-lab-fr3-fr1-validation.sh (fr3.production_conversion verdict). Remaining scope: SMB/S3 per-op stay ASSUMED, VolumeMetrics unit unproven (volume scope queryable, values null in the sampled window).

2026-08-17: DONE. The actionable defect (host_view ~1000x) is fixed and real-VMS validated; remaining sources are recorded at their honest confidence with no code change warranted. Contradictory future evidence opens a new FR, not this one.

items.title: Exporter scrape responsiveness
items.summary: Determine with measurement whether the synchronous exporter scrape causes objectionable TUI stalls; do not change architecture on this FR alone.
scope: Measure scrape duration.
Measure the input/UI stall attributable to the scrape.
Determine whether synchronous behavior is acceptable.
If unacceptable, stop and present evidence before any architecture change.
acceptance_criteria: Either synchronous scrape responsiveness is demonstrated acceptable, or evidence justifies an explicitly approved asynchronous design.
evidence: Observed exporter scrape cost approximately 1.2-2.4 s on drill entry.
Whether that is actually unacceptable in practice remains unresolved.
notes: Background threading/concurrency is an L1 architectural decision; do NOT implement threading merely because this FR exists. Measure first.

scope: Add Windows execution/build coverage where practical.

Catch platform-specific packaging/runtime defects.

items.title: Protocol API-efficiency re-audit
items.summary: Establish a fresh post-refactor API-cost baseline for all five engines; audit only, no optimization in this FR.
scope: Measure NFSv3, NFSv4.1, SMB, S3 and NVMe/TCP.
Capture startup calls, startup monitor creates, and time to first usable screen.
Capture normal refresh calls and steady-state query rate.
Capture drill-entry calls, drill-entry monitor creates, and drill steady-state calls.
Capture cleanup calls and create/delete balance.
Identify remaining O(N) paths and the largest remaining API consumers.
acceptance_criteria: A ranked, evidence-backed inventory of remaining performance/API costs from which future optimization FRs can be created.
evidence: The instrumented mock (tests/mock_vms.py) records every call and is the measurement instrument.
Round-5B whole-session NVMe baseline: 140 calls, 20 creates, 20 deletes, 95 queries.
notes: Audit first. Do not turn this directly into an optimization pass.

items.title: Release / product hardening
items.summary: Make opstat cleanly installable, documented, packaged and releasable from a fresh environment on supported systems.
scope: CLI consistency and help accuracy.
README reconciliation and documentation cleanup.
Narrow-terminal visual sweep and resize behavior.
Clean install/bootstrap and packaging validation.
Upgrade sanity and backward-compatibility sanity.
Windows packaging.
Final release gate and versioning/release preparation.
acceptance_criteria: Supported systems can install and run opstat from a clean environment.
Packaging is repeatably validated and the release gate is green.
evidence: 2026-08-18 (manual-testing pass, measured on the mock and with realistic lab values; NOT a real-VMS observation): the NVMe header lines are printed WITHOUT truncation - nvme_tcp._render_frame prints `title` and the `Cluster ... VMS ... Refresh ...` meta line directly, unlike nfs_v41 which truncates both explicitly (nfs_v41.py:2200-2206, comment: 'Header lines sit outside the box borders, so they must be truncated explicitly'). Measured widths of the NVMe meta line: 79 columns with the short mock cluster name, and 112 columns with realistic lab values (cluster selab-var-203, VMS var203.selab.vastdata.com:443, OS label release-5.4.6-2628322) - so it overflows a STANDARD 80-column terminal, not merely very narrow ones. This corrects the first framing of the observation ('around 40 columns and below'), which came from a mock run with a short hostname. The 'Waiting for data...' line (60 columns) and, below ~30 columns, the title line overflow too. An overflowing header wraps and shifts every row beneath it, which is the frame-corruption mode the box renderers already guard against.

2026-08-18: the defect is NOT NVMe-only. Same probe at 80/60/40 columns: nvme_tcp overflows (max 112), nfs_v3 overflows (max 99), nfs_v41 is clean at every width (it truncates). smb and s3 print their title and sample/frame/source lines untruncated in the same shape (smb.py:2246-2252, s3.py:2190-2196) so they are very likely affected, but this pass could NOT measure them - both raised KeyError rendering without fuller row state, so treat smb/s3 as unverified rather than confirmed. Coverage explains why this survived: a whole-frame width invariant exists only for nfs_v41 (tests/test_render_navigation.py test_frame_never_exceeds_the_terminal_width); no equivalent exists for nvme/nfs_v3/smb/s3. A fix should pair header truncation with that invariant test per engine.

2026-08-25 SCOPE ITEM 3 (narrow-terminal visual sweep) IMPLEMENTED, mock-proven, NOT real-VMS validated. Audit drove all five REAL engines against the mock with realistic values (cluster selab-var-203, VMS var203.selab.vastdata.com:443, build release-5.4.6-2628322) across dashboard / startup / drill-loading / drill-error / waiting frames at 160/120/100/80/60/40/24 columns, measuring every line with display_width. Result BEFORE: nfs_v3 and nvme_tcp overflowed from 100 columns down (max 99 and 114); smb and s3 overflowed from 80 down (max 100 and 99) - this CONFIRMS the previously unproven smb/s3 status; nfs_v41 was clean. Root causes: header/meta lines drawn outside the box machinery were never truncated, box titles were never truncated (overflow below ~26 columns), and NFSv3's COMBINED grand-total line is also drawn outside the boxes. ADDITIONAL DEFECT FOUND IN THE SHARED HELPER: tui_layout.truncate_display counted ANSI escape BYTES against the width budget and could cut mid-escape - with colour on (the real terminal default) an 80-column NFSv4.1 header rendered only 50 visible columns, silently dropping the cluster name, and a cut inside an escape emitted a broken sequence. So the 'known-good' nfs_v41 precedent was correct only with colour disabled. Fix: truncate_display is now ANSI-aware (escapes pass through at zero cost, never split, styling closed with a reset), and the four engines truncate their out-of-box header/meta/status/total lines and box titles using that same existing idiom. Result AFTER: all five engines clean at every audited width, colour on and off. No telemetry, API, monitor-lifecycle or refresh behaviour changed. tests/test_frame_width.py (51 cases) drives real engines against the mock and pins the invariant per engine, per state, per width, in both colour modes; proven to fail before the fix (28 of 51 failed on the pre-fix tree). tests/test_tui_layout.py gained 5 ANSI-truncation cases. Gate: 902 passed / 0 failed / 0 skipped on current Python and 3.8.

2026-08-25 REVIEW PASS on the width work (3 read-only specialist reviews of 6aced47; fixes in 93313fd). TUI/ANSI and cross-protocol: no blocking findings. Test-quality: five blocking, all verified real and fixed - a circular engine-coverage guard, a colour test comparing only line 0 (vacuous for 4 of 5 engines, and a width bound cannot substitute because the escape-budget bug made lines NARROWER), a reset test that never reached its branch, a vacuous telemetry guard for dict-backed engines, and an overstated coverage claim in the durable rule file. The strengthened colour test then caught a REAL pre-existing defect: with colour on the NFSv4.1 footer showed '[d] Delegatio...' at 80 columns, because str.rstrip() leaves a trailing space that sits before a reset escape, costing a display column; fixed with ANSI-aware tui_layout.rstrip_display in the three legend builders. EVIDENCE CORRECTION: 6aced47 recorded 114/99-column overflows measured with the BUILD id in CLUSTER_OS, which the header does not render; re-measured with the observed dotted sw_version shape the widest pre-fix lines are 101 (nfs_v3), 100 (nvme_tcp), 99 (smb), 98 (s3) - still overflowing a standard 80-column terminal, so the defect stands but the earlier magnitudes were inflated. 48 of the 107 cases in the two suites fail on a d527ddc worktree. Gate: 944 passed / 0 failed / 0 skipped on current Python and 3.8.

2026-08-25 SCOPE ITEMS 1 (CLI consistency / help accuracy) and 2 (README reconciliation) COMPLETE. Inventory taken from the parser, not the docs: 31 options, 29 visible, 2 hidden (--port, --no-menu), 3 multi-spelling actions (-h/--help, --menu/-i, -V/--tool-version) plus four singular/plural scoping alias pairs. DRIFT AND DECISIONS: (a) --no-menu was implemented, behaviour-tested (tests/test_wizard.py) and documented in README's user-facing table and an example, yet SUPPRESSed from --help - resolved as Option A, EXPOSED, because every other signal says user-facing and wizard.should_launch treats it as a documented control; (b) --port is an undocumented compatibility alias for --vms-port kept HIDDEN (two visible spellings of one option is the drift being removed) with the rationale, the load-bearing declaration order and a parse-level test now recorded; (c) README claimed --log-api-calls redacts secrets - there is no redaction code; credentials are never written because auth lives in headers that log_call never receives, while cluster identifiers ARE written; (d) --password's runtime warning and VAST_TOKEN's precedence over --password were undocumented; (e) '--menu # force wizard' overstated (it still requires a TTY); (f) NVMe naming and the repository-layout list corrected. parse_args was split into build_parser() + parse_args - structurally proven behaviour-preserving: a full action/group/mutex dump differs in exactly one boolean, --no-menu's help visibility. NEW GUARD tests/test_cli_contract.py (22 cases) derives options from build_parser() and holds --help and README's tables to them, with an allowlist that catches both undeclared hidden options and stale entries; it fails on the original --no-menu drift. Two read-only reviews: CLI/parser no blocking or high; doc/test-contract no blocking, three HIGH (mutation-proven vacuous version, required-ness and NFS-status assertions) all fixed, plus value-level guards for documented defaults. Collection floor raised 712 -> 885 per the gate's own policy. Gate: 966 passed / 0 failed / 0 skipped on current Python and 3.8. Packaged-executable behaviour was NOT exercised in this slice.

2026-08-25 VERSION / RELEASE-METADATA CONSISTENCY (scope item 7 groundwork; no version bump, no tag, no release). AUDIT: there was NO authoritative version - VERSION = '0.1.2' was declared six times (the opstat entrypoint plus all five engines), agreeing only by luck, while three engines' own header comments still said 0.1.1. No pyproject/setup metadata exists. build_opstat.py never used the version (artifact names are opstat-<os>-<arch>, version-free). RELEASE RISK FOUND: .github/workflows/release.yml triggers on v* and never read VERSION, so pushing v9.9.9 would have run tests, built Linux/macOS/Windows binaries and published a GitHub Release whose artifacts report opstat 0.1.2, with nothing to stop it. FIX: new import-safe opstat_version.py is the single source (no imports, no side effects - the entrypoint is extensionless, so tooling cannot import IT to read a version without running the program); entrypoint and all five engines now derive VERSION and the stale header comments are gone; scripts/check_version_contract.py enforces tag vX.Y.Z == VERSION and is wired into the release workflow's test job, which build needs and publish needs transitively, so a mismatch fails before anything is built or published; opstat_version added to the packaging hidden imports. Checkpoint tags remain outside the release namespace (checkpoint-0.1.2-refactor-complete does not match v*) and the gate refuses them explicitly if passed by hand. Runtime unchanged: -V and --tool-version both print opstat 0.1.2. README now documents the version source and a generic 'git tag vX.Y.Z' procedure. tests/test_version_contract.py (35 cases) pins single-sourcing, runtime output, the tag gate incl. exit status, workflow wiring and ordering, trigger scope, packaging, and active doc claims - while explicitly protecting historical references ('pre-v0.1.2 UI', the captured lab frame) from an over-eager future sweep. Gate: 1001 passed / 0 failed / 0 skipped on current Python and 3.8. NOT done: no release was built or published, and packaged-executable behaviour remains unexercised.

2026-08-25 REVIEW PASS on the version slice (2 read-only reviews). Release/versioning: no blocking, 2 HIGH - a surviving '(v0.1.2)' literal in the opstat header comment, and the discovery that tag v0.1.2 IS ALREADY PUBLISHED on origin (pointing at an old commit), so the gate's one permitted tag is taken and the next release must begin with a version bump; moving a published tag is prohibited. Test-contract: 2 BLOCKING - the workflow guards were raw substring checks over YAML text, so COMMENTING OUT the gate step left the suite green, and the trigger test read only the FIRST tags entry, so adding '- checkpoint-*' went unnoticed; plus HIGH - the comment scan keyed on the CURRENT version, firing while a comment was correct and going silent once it went stale (the literal 0.1.1 defect this slice cites). All fixed: workflow assertions are now comment-aware, parse every trigger entry, and tolerate YAML reformatting and job reordering; the prose scan flags version claims by SHAPE across root and scripts/; doc claims are swept across all markdown instead of an allowlist; historical protection is driven from the HISTORICAL constant; mismatch tags are derived from VERSION rather than hardcoded; the gate no longer advises re-tagging a published tag and now warns when v<VERSION> already exists; publish re-verifies immediately before publication; README and the workflow header state the trigger accurately (v*, gated to vX.Y.Z) and record both the taken-tag fact and the tagging-an-old-commit caveat. Every previously-undetected mutation is now caught. Collection floor 885 -> 920. Gate: 1004 passed / 0 failed / 0 skipped on current Python and 3.8.

2026-08-25 CLEAN INSTALL / PACKAGING VALIDATION. Host: macOS arm64 (Darwin 25.5.0), Python 3.12.13, PyInstaller 6.22.2, in a fresh venv containing only pip. CLEAN BOOTSTRAP = DONE: requirements.txt's stdlib-only runtime claim is PROVEN - the source CLI ran (-V, --tool-version, --help, -h all rc=0) with zero pip installs; no undocumented dependency exists, and pyinstaller>=6.0 is the only build dependency. REAL BUILD = DONE: `python scripts/build_opstat.py` (the committed path the release workflow also uses) produced releases/opstat-macos-arm64, 9.2 MB, executable, in 3-4 s, rc=0, with no warning naming any first-party module; the PyInstaller warn report is 22 lines listing only Windows-only stdlib (winreg, nt, _winapi, msvcrt) and importlib internals - no first-party module. BUNDLE AUDIT settles the open review question: all 14 first-party modules are in the bundle, and vast_drill, vast_discovery and nfs4_native - absent from HIDDEN_IMPORTS - are bundled by static analysis alone. Every one of the 11 HIDDEN_IMPORTS entries is in fact redundant; nothing was added prophylactically. PACKAGED SMOKE = DONE: run from a scratch directory with the source tree unreachable and PYTHONPATH cleared, the artifact reports 'opstat 0.1.2' for both spellings, --help/-h rc=0, missing --vms exits 2, protocol validation runs, no ModuleNotFoundError, and a MANUAL run dispatched into the SMB engine far enough to render a real TUI frame (INITIALIZING panel), proving smb/tui_layout/vast_common/vast_drill work packaged - that observation is one-off and deliberately NOT reproduced by the committed smoke script, which stops before dispatch so it can never open a network connection in CI. SOURCE vs PACKAGED: --help BYTE-IDENTICAL, same version, identical exit codes across parser-failure cases (2 for a missing --vms, 1 for the protocol-validation failures). BUILD-SCRIPT DEFECT FOUND AND FIXED: dist/ is not cleared by --clean, so with PyInstaller exiting 0 but writing nothing the PREVIOUS dist/opstat was copied to releases/ and reported as 'Created' with exit 0 - a stale binary presented as a successful build, which a release would publish. Now refused deterministically: the expected output is DELETED before PyInstaller runs, so its reappearance is the proof of freshness (reproduced, then verified refused). An mtime-versus-wall-clock comparison was implemented first and rejected on review - it would falsely refuse a legitimate --no-clean rebuild, where PyInstaller reuses an unchanged EXE, and is sensitive to filesystem timestamp granularity and clock skew. PyInstaller failure propagation was already correct. GUARDS: tests/test_packaging_contract.py (23 cheap cases: artifact naming per platform, workflow/script name agreement, hidden-import validity, static-reachability of every first-party module, no dynamic first-party import, failure propagation, stale and empty artifact refusal, no hardcoded version, workflow builds via the committed script and smoke-tests before upload) plus scripts/smoke_packaged_opstat.py, which is deliberately NOT a pytest test (it needs a real build) and is wired into every release-workflow build leg before upload. Gate: 1027 passed / 0 failed / 0 skipped on current Python and 3.8; collection floor raised 920 -> 945. STATUS: clean install/bootstrap DONE; packaging validation DONE for macOS arm64; Linux and Windows packaging UNVALIDATED (built by the same script in CI but never executed here - Windows execution belongs to FR5 and was not consumed into FR7).

2026-08-25 REVIEW PASS on the packaging slice (2 read-only reviews, 29 and 12 mutations). No blocking; 6 HIGH, all fixed. Packaging review: the mtime freshness check was clock-dependent and would have falsely refused a --no-clean rebuild (replaced with pre-build deletion); one smoke assertion was vacuous because '--nvme-over-tcp' appears in argparse's usage banner, so it passed on any parser failure (now asserts rc==1 and a message fragment that cannot appear in usage). Test-contract review: the artifact-naming test read the workflow RAW, so a commented-out Windows matrix leg passed - the same defect class the version slice had already fixed elsewhere; the smoke-step test compared line positions only, so 'if: false', '|| true', a trailing-comment mention and a second uploading job all passed; and NOTHING parsed the smoke script, so a syntax error left the whole suite green and would have surfaced in CI after three builds. Now: comments are stripped whole-line AND trailing, an indentation-aware step scanner asserts every uploading job smoke-tests first with no 'if:' and no exit-status swallowing, the matrix legs are pinned, and the smoke script is AST-parsed with its non-zero-exit path and exact version comparison asserted. Also added: PyInstaller invocation flags pinned (--onefile, --paths, one --hidden-import per entry, entrypoint last), HIDDEN_IMPORTS asserted non-empty, build.sh and build.bat asserted to delegate to build_opstat.py, and the NOT_BUNDLED allowlist asserted to stay empty so narrowing the bundle guarantee cannot be a silent one-line edit. Every previously-uncaught mutation is now caught. ACCEPTED RISK, recorded rather than mitigated: the smoke step runs on all three release legs and publish needs build, so a bug in the smoke script itself could block a release; it has only ever executed on macOS arm64. Windows execution remains FR5's.

2026-08-25 RESIZE / SIGWINCH - scope item 3's remaining half, measured in a real pty on macOS arm64 (Python 3.12.13). ARCHITECTURE: all five engines read the width INSIDE _render_frame (never cached); height is unused (.lines appears nowhere), so LINES is immaterial; no SIGWINCH handler exists anywhere - only SIGINT/SIGTERM/SIGHUP are installed. DEFECT FOUND AND FIXED (correctness): shutil.get_terminal_size honours COLUMNS BEFORE the ioctl, so an exported stale COLUMNS pinned the width permanently. Measured pre-fix against a RUNNING opstat resized 120 -> 80 -> 40 -> 120 with COLUMNS=200: it NEVER converged, emitting 120-column frames into an 80- and then a 40-column terminal indefinitely - wrapping and corrupting the display, the exact failure the FR7 width sweep exists to prevent. With COLUMNS unset the same sequence converged every time in 2.45/4.89/5.10 s at --refresh 5 AGAINST THE IN-PROCESS MOCK (~ms loopback), no keypress, no over-wide frame emitted, footer intact. The real bound is one refresh interval plus the in-flight fetch, because guarded_poll renders after fetching - on a live cluster a poll cycle is several monitor queries at seconds each, so expect up to a full cycle. That is latency, not correctness. FIX: new vast_common.terminal_width(fallback, cap) asks the tty's own file descriptor and falls back to shutil only when no stream is a terminal (pipes and the render suites, where honouring COLUMNS is correct); the five engines now call it. Post-fix the stale-COLUMNS case converges identically to the clean case (2.44/4.89/5.10 s). SIGWINCH DECISION: NOT ADDED, and not needed - correctness is restored by the width source, latency is bounded by the existing refresh interval, and no signal-handler work is required; adding one would only shave <= REFRESH_SECONDS off an already-correct repaint. COVERAGE: tests/test_terminal_resize.py commits the PTY harness (bounded waits, unconditional child teardown, complete-frame parsing) - 9 cases resizing the SAME running process, plus width-source cases. Mutation-proven: on the pre-fix tree 6 of 9 fail; with the helper present but engines still calling shutil, the engine integration case fails. One engine is driven end to end (SMB) because the width source, render loop and repaint mechanism are shared verbatim by all five, and each engine's own renderer is already width-pinned by tests/test_frame_width.py at 24-160 columns. PLATFORM BOUNDARY: pty.fork is POSIX-only; the gate runs macOS + ubuntu-latest so the guard never fires there, and Windows terminal behaviour remains FR5's, unvalidated here.

2026-08-25 REVIEW PASS on the resize slice. PTY/signal review: no blocking, 6 HIGH, all fixed. (1) The width change made the existing width/nav suites depend on pytest's capture mode - under `pytest -s` in a terminal sys.__stdout__ IS the tty, so the suites' shutil monkeypatch was bypassed and they rendered at the real terminal width; reproduced, then fixed by patching the real seam (vast_common.terminal_width) in all four render helpers. (2) Only SMB was driven end-to-end and only its stale-COLUMNS case could tell the two width sources apart, so reverting any of the other four engines would have left the suite green - now pinned by a per-engine source assertion. (3) The POSIX skip marker could never fire: module-level fcntl/pty/termios imports made Windows a collection ERROR aborting the session, not the documented skip - now importorskip. (4) On the 3.8 floor shutil does NOT coalesce a 0-column winsize to the fallback (3.11+ does), so terminal_width could return 0 on a 0x0 pty - now coalesced explicitly. (5) stderr was consulted, so piping the frame to a file while stderr stayed on a terminal took the tty path, contradicting the documented contract - stderr removed. (6) The convergence figures were mock-derived and stated unqualified, which the evidence rule forbids - now qualified in both the rule and the evidence above. Also: dead shutil imports removed from all five engines, the rule's claim that the suite would catch a SIGWINCH handler corrected (it would only converge faster), fixture registered before entering to close a leak window, the W= regex anchored, and the collection floor raised 945 -> 955. Final gate: 1042 passed / 0 failed / 0 skipped on current Python and 3.8, collected 1042 against floor 955. REVIEWER OUTCOMES: PTY/signal completed (6 HIGH, all fixed). The test-quality reviewer was killed mid-run but had already published its mutation table, and one result was a REAL uncaught gap: M3 - a mutation where the width can narrow but never widen back - SURVIVED, because converge() accepted any frame <= target, so after 40 -> 120 a stale 40-column frame 'converged' instantly. Fixed: convergence now requires the frame to actually USE the new width (exactly min(target, cap)), and the M3 mutation is now caught (both engine resize cases fail). The cross-engine reviewer stalled after 600s with no output and was not replaced; that analysis was done directly instead - all five engines share one width source, one guarded_poll repaint tick and one wait_for_input, and each engine's renderer is width-pinned at 24-160 columns by tests/test_frame_width.py.
notes: 2026-08-18: scoped into this FR rather than given its own number - 'Narrow-terminal visual sweep and resize behavior' is already FR7 scope, and the backlog rule allocates a new FR only for genuinely new work. Not implemented in the manual-testing pass: it is pre-existing, affects normal dashboard frames as well as drill frames, and touches four engines' renderers plus new per-engine width tests - too broad to fix opportunistically inside a UI-classification change.

2026-08-25: FR7 REMAINS IN_PROGRESS. Only scope item 3 (narrow-terminal visual sweep and resize behavior) is addressed, and only its width half - resize behaviour under a live SIGWINCH is unproven because no committed harness drives a PTY. Untouched: item 1 CLI consistency and help accuracy; item 2 README reconciliation; item 4 clean install/bootstrap and packaging validation; item 5 upgrade and backward-compatibility sanity; item 6 Windows packaging (overlaps FR5, which owns Windows execution/build coverage); item 7 final release gate and versioning. Those are separate hardening activities - packaging and install validation need a clean environment and, for Windows, CI that FR5 has to establish first - so they cannot be completed honestly in a rendering pass. Real-VMS confirmation of the width sweep on a live terminal is also still outstanding.

2026-08-25: scope items 1 and 2 are complete. FR7 REMAINS in_progress - item 3's resize/SIGWINCH half, and items 4 (clean install/bootstrap and packaging validation), 5 (upgrade/backward-compatibility sanity), 6 (Windows packaging, which needs FR5's Windows CI first) and 7 (final release gate and versioning) are untouched.

2026-08-25: version/release-metadata consistency complete. FR7 REMAINS in_progress - item 3's resize/SIGWINCH half, item 4 (clean install/bootstrap and packaging validation), item 5 (upgrade/backward-compatibility sanity), item 6 (Windows packaging, behind FR5) and the rest of item 7 (actually exercising a release end to end) are open.

2026-08-25: scope item 4 (clean install/bootstrap + packaging validation) is DONE for the host platform and the bootstrap contract, PARTIAL across platforms (macOS arm64 validated; Linux/Windows unexecuted). FR7 REMAINS in_progress: item 3's resize/SIGWINCH half, item 5 (upgrade/backward-compatibility sanity), item 6 (Windows packaging, behind FR5) and the rest of item 7 (an end-to-end release, which needs a version-bump decision) are open.

2026-08-25: scope item 3 is now COMPLETE - the width sweep and the resize half are both done and PTY-measured. FR7 REMAINS in_progress: item 4 is partial (macOS arm64 packaging validated; Linux/Windows built but unexecuted), item 5 (upgrade/backward-compatibility sanity) is open and currently unexercisable because the only published release is v0.1.2 on an old commit, item 6 (Windows packaging) is behind FR5, and item 7 needs an end-to-end release, which needs a version-bump decision.

items.title: Validation tooling disposition
items.summary: Decide deliberately which refactor-era probe/validator machinery becomes permanent, and archive or remove the rest safely.
scope: Inventory probe/validator machinery.
Retain reusable regression tooling.
Distinguish CI tests from real-VMS diagnostics.
Identify one-off forensic scripts.
Remove/archive obsolete machinery safely.
Prevent the repository from becoming a museum of every investigation ever performed.
acceptance_criteria: Validation tooling has a deliberate permanent structure.
evidence: scripts/var203_validation/ carries the round-1..5B validator and probes; some parts are durable regression tooling, some were forensic one-offs.

items.title: Validator attribution polish
items.summary: Fix the two non-blocking Round-5B attribution imperfections found in the raw API log; validator precision only, not production defects.
scope: Make no-telemetry completion scope-aware or require a fresh repaint so consecutive dead-scope notices cannot cross-match.
Tighten manual-refresh throttle-window attribution against mid-burst latency gaps.
Improve quiet detection so one slow in-flight call is not mistaken for a quiet interval.
acceptance_criteria: Validator attribution matches raw API chronology without relying on residual screen state or ambiguous burst reconstruction.
evidence: Round-5B HOST row reported 2 calls / 0 creates because residual VIP-notice text matched the scope-agnostic marker; raw-log truth was 4 calls / 1 create.
Round-5B manual-refresh PASS cited a throttle-window query that was actually part of the in-flight cadence burst; the verdict was independently correct via the abort/restart evidence.
Round-5B verdict is accepted; these are precision improvements only.

items.title: Drill input responsiveness refinement
items.summary: Evaluate whether the drill-query loop should become input-aware like the headline loop; measure first, refine only if users experience the bounded latency as objectionable.
scope: Measure actual drill input latency.
Determine whether users experience it as objectionable.
If worthwhile, design the smallest safe interruptible-query refinement.
acceptance_criteria: Either the existing bounded latency is accepted with evidence, or an evidence-backed refinement is implemented and validated.
evidence: Worst-case keypress latency inside a drill is approximately one drill-query set, roughly 15-50 s on var203.
x works within budget; this is not a correctness defect.

items.title: Startup-loading UX as general invariant
items.summary: Decide whether the startup loading-frame pattern should be codified as a formal invariant for future engines/features, or whether current rule coverage already suffices.
scope: Inspect existing rule coverage (.claude/rules/tui-behavior.md).
Determine whether the pattern is already sufficiently codified.
Promote it to a durable invariant only if useful.
acceptance_criteria: Explicit decision to either codify the pattern generally or leave current behavior as sufficient.
evidence: Carried from the milestone closeout's open decision note (open decision #6 in REFACTOR_HANDOFF).

items.title: Future monitor consolidation re-evaluation
items.summary: Revisit cross-family/headline monitor consolidation only when VAST API behavior changes; the current split is evidence-backed and consolidation is ruled out on var203/5.4.6.
scope: Re-probe merge legality when a new VAST release provides new evidence.
Only then evaluate whether consolidation is legal and beneficial.
acceptance_criteria: A future VAST release provides new evidence that consolidation is legal and beneficial; otherwise remain deferred.
evidence: var203 VAST OS 5.4.6 rejects the attempted property combinations at query time (HTTP 400 "can't mix properties").
Cross-family behavior has been build-inconsistent.
notes: Do not spend current engineering time forcing this.
